title: Devils acquire winger Evangelista from Predators on September 1
dek: New Jersey traded a conditional 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Nashville for 24-year-old winger Luke Evangelista on September 1. Evangelista recorded 56 points last season and ranked fourth in scoring for the Predators. The trade marks GM Sunny Mehta's second major scoring addition alongside free-agent signing Anthony Mantha.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Devils acquired winger Luke Evangelista from Nashville on September 1, 2026, in exchange for a conditional 2028 first-rounder and a 2028 second-rounder.
bottom_line: Evangelista's durability and the sustainability of his 24-point improvement will define whether New Jersey's gamble on a young talent justifies the conditional draft capital surrendered. The condition's specific triggers (Colorado's draft movements and pick placement) will determine the actual value exchanged by the time future picks are made.
body: The New Jersey Devils acquired winger Luke Evangelista from the Nashville Predators on September 1, 2026, in exchange for a conditional 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, per Yahoo Sports.

Evangelista, 24, recorded 56 points (12 goals, 44 assists) in the most recent season, marking a 24-point increase from his prior year. He ranked fourth in scoring and second in assists for the Predators. The 2020 second-round pick, 42nd overall, is in the second year of a two-year, $6 million contract and will become a restricted free agent after the season.

The conditional nature of the first-rounder introduces complexity: it remains the Colorado Avalanche's 2028 pick unless either Colorado's 2027 first-round pick is not transferred to Toronto or Colorado's 2028 first-round pick falls within the top 10, at which point it becomes a 2029 first-round pick.

Evangelista's 56 points would have placed him fourth on the Devils' roster last season, when New Jersey ranked 27th in team scoring. GM Sunny Mehta has now added scoring from the wing through both this acquisition and the recent signing of free-agent Anthony Mantha, a 33-goal scorer.

Nashville's GM Chris MacFarland, while calling the trade "not an easy decision," justified the move by citing new forwards added this offseason (Mavrik Bourque, Ross Colton, and Jack Drury) and the organizational opportunity created. The Predators now hold seven picks in the first two rounds over the next two drafts, per Yahoo Sports.
Yahoo Sports assigned the Devils a trade grade of B and the Predators a grade of C+.
